title: Use strong identity and least-privilege access
description: Prefer centralized identity, strong authentication, short-lived credentials, and least-privilege authorization.

title: Protect secrets and sensitive configuration
description: Keep secrets out of source code and use managed secret storage with rotation.

title: Encrypt data in transit and at rest
description: Use modern encryption for data flows and stored data, with appropriate key management.

title: Segment networks and workloads
description: Limit lateral movement with segmentation, explicit trust boundaries, and restrictive traffic policies.

title: Design for failure isolation
description: Reduce blast radius by isolating failure domains, tenants, components, or cells where appropriate.

title: Automate backup and recovery
description: Use automated, monitored backups and define recovery objectives.

title: Test recovery procedures
description: Regularly validate failover, restore, and disaster-recovery procedures instead of relying on documentation alone.

title: Use resilient communication patterns
description: Apply timeouts, retries with backoff, idempotency, and circuit breaking where appropriate.

title: Scale capacity according to demand
description: Use elasticity or autoscaling where workloads have variable demand.

title: Measure end-to-end performance
description: Collect latency, throughput, saturation, and error signals for critical user journeys and services.

title: Use caching intentionally
description: Cache suitable data and responses while defining expiration, invalidation, and consistency behavior.

title: Select fit-for-purpose managed services
description: Prefer services whose operational and scaling characteristics match the workload requirements.

title: Track cost ownership
description: Use tagging, accounts, subscriptions, projects, or equivalent structures to attribute cloud spend.

title: Right-size resources
description: Regularly compare provisioned capacity with observed utilization and workload requirements.

title: Remove idle and obsolete resources
description: Detect and retire unused compute, storage, addresses, snapshots, and other billable resources.

title: Use lifecycle and retention policies
description: Align storage tiers, logs, backups, and retained data with actual business and compliance requirements.

title: Improve workload utilization
description: Reduce unnecessary resource consumption by increasing utilization efficiency and eliminating idle capacity.

title: Minimize unnecessary data movement
description: Reduce avoidable network transfers, duplicate processing, and excessive data replication.

title: Use efficient data retention
description: Avoid retaining unnecessary data and choose storage classes appropriate to access patterns.

title: Consider sustainability in architecture decisions
description: Include energy, resource efficiency, and environmental impact among architecture trade-offs where data is available.
